question: Zheng He began his first voyage to the “Western Seas” to promote tributary trade to Ming China.
Johannes Gutenberg developed a movable-type printing press in Europe, accelerating the spread of books and ideas.
Sultan Mehmet II conquered the Byzantine capital of Constantinople, renaming it Istanbul.
Christopher Columbus reached the Bahamas, beginning sustained European contact with the Americas.
Spain and Portugal signed the Treaty of Tordesillas, dividing their claims in the Americas.
Vasco da Gama reached India, establishing a Portuguese sea route to South Asia.
Sikhism emerged in South Asia from interactions between Hinduism and Islam.
Ismail I founded the Safavid Empire and established Twelver Shi’a Islam as its state religion.
The Portuguese captured Goa, establishing a major base in the Indian Ocean.
Martin Luther published his Ninety-Five Theses, beginning the Protestant Reformation.
Sultan Selim I conquered Egypt and the holy cities of Mecca and Medina reinforcing his claim as caliph.
Hernán Cortés and his Indigenous allies conquered the Aztec Empire for Spain.
Babur defeated the Delhi Sultanate and established the Mughal Empire in India.
Francisco Pizarro and his Indigenous allies conquered the Inca Empire for Spain.
The discovery of Potosí made Spanish America a major source of silver.
European colonists expanded sugar plantations that increasingly relied on enslaved African labor.
Under Ivan IV, Russia conquered Kazan and Astrakhan, beginning major expansion into Eurasia.
Spain established Manila, connecting American silver with Asian markets.
The Ming government required many taxes to be paid in silver, increasing China's participation in global trade.
Russia expanded across Siberia, greatly increasing the territory of the Russian Empire.
Moroccan forces defeated the Songhai Empire at the Battle of Tondibi, weakening Songhai power in West Africa.
Spanish America developed a racial caste system distinguishing peninsulares, creoles, mestizos, and other groups.
The Dutch East India Company was established as a powerful joint-stock trading company.
The Tokugawa shogunate unified Japan and gradually restricted foreign trade.
Samuel de Champlain founded Quebec, strengthening French colonization of North America.
Michael Romanov became czar, beginning the Romanov dynasty that would rule Russia for centuries.
Enslaved Africans arrived in English North America, contributing to the growth of racialized slavery.
Queen Nzinga resisted Portuguese expansion while ruling Ndongo and later Matamba in Central Africa.
Shah Jahan began construction of the Taj Mahal as a mausoleum for his deceased wife.
Peasant rebellions weakened the Ming Dynasty as Manchu forces seized Beijing and established the Qing Dynasty.
Dutch settlers established a colony at the Cape of Good Hope, strengthening European influence in southern Africa.
The Marathas established an independent state under Shivaji, challenging Mughal power in India.
Metacom's War erupted between Indigenous peoples and English colonists in New England.
The Pueblo Revolt temporarily drove the Spanish from New Mexico.
The Glorious Revolution strengthened Parliament and limited the power of the English monarchy.
Under Peter the Great, Russia gained territory on the Baltic Sea after defeating Sweden.
Yongzheng became Qing emperor and strengthened central administration and government finances.
European states increasingly used mercantilism and joint-stock companies to compete for global trade and colonies.
The Asante Empire expanded in West Africa through control of gold and participation in Atlantic trade.
